channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: SACP Ideology Hinders Electoral Prospects
item.description: The South African Communist Party's adherence to socialist principles may limit its appeal to voters disillusioned with the ANC in upcoming municipal elections.

item.title: Women miners face rape and harassment in Sierra Leone's Kono district
item.description: Artisanal miners in Kono recount sexual violence and lack of recourse after reporting incidents to mine authorities.

item.title: Finance Minister Defends Economic Management Amidst Criticism
item.description: A coalition of civil society groups called for the finance minister's dismissal, but the ministry argues global shocks, not local mismanagement, caused hardship.

item.title: Sierra Leone Vice Presidency Fails to Produce Presidents
item.description: The constitutionally powerful office has historically served as a political cul-de-sac, with no vice president ever elected to the presidency.

item.title: Charcoal burning deforests Sierra Leone, threatens food security
item.description: Environmental officials warn that the widespread practice of charcoal production is leading to deforestation and the loss of economic trees, impacting climate and food.

item.title: Enugu Police Arrest 6,240 Suspects, Rescue 211 Kidnap Victims
item.description: The Enugu State Police Command reported arresting 6,240 suspects and recovering 156 firearms in 17 months of operations.

item.title: Advocate Seeks High Risk Framework After Child's Death
item.description: A civic advocate is calling for a coordinated system to identify and act on domestic violence risk signals following a child's death.

item.title: Candidates Selected for Demographic Ratios, Not Competence
item.description: Mauritian political parties prioritize fitting demographic profiles over policy expertise when selecting candidates for constituencies.

item.title: Government Revives Civic Education Program for 200 Students
item.description: Mauritius relaunches the National Initiative for Civic Education (NICE) program, aiming to instill patriotism and civic values in young citizens.

item.title: Ghana Maritime Authority readies oil-spill vessel
item.description: The "MV Esther Ocloo" is now operationally ready for deployment after a ten-day training program to protect offshore oil and gas assets.

item.title: Malema Promises R4,500 Old-Age Grant
item.description: The EFF leader pledged to more than double the current R2,400 monthly grant if his party wins upcoming local government elections.

item.title: Campaign Mobilizes Citizens for Cleanup Ahead of Inauguration
item.description: The 'Kwa ti Kodro' operation saw ruling party affiliates cleaning public spaces in Grand Bangui and other cities.

item.title: Queer Namibians Face Escalating Violence, Demand Government Protection
item.description: A former Mr. Gay Namibia contestant writes from abroad, detailing a wave of hate crimes and urging lawmakers to enact hate crime legislation.

item.title: Malawi Faces K324.8 Billion El Niño Funding Gap
item.description: A shortfall of K324.8 billion threatens national resilience efforts across food security, energy, health, and water systems.

item.title: Ghana Upgrades Rural Telecom Sites to 4G
item.description: Government aims to bridge the digital divide by enhancing connectivity in underserved areas with faster mobile technology.

item.title: Speaker's Ad Hoc Committees Face Legal Challenge
item.description: A private citizen has obtained a court injunction halting parliamentary inquiries into state bodies until the High Court clarifies legislative powers.

item.title: Opposition Leader Contests Security Claims
item.description: Raymond Adouma stated that the pacification claimed by President Touadéra exists only in speeches, not in reality for citizens.

item.title: Botswana Groceries Outsell South African Prices on Select Items
item.description: A comparison of nine everyday grocery items reveals that Botswana's prices are lower for flour, chicken, pasta, and sugar.

item.title: Malian Anti-Corruption Network Seeks Public Contract Audit
item.description: A coalition of anti-corruption groups has formally requested a review of public contracts awarded during the nation's six-year military transition period.

item.title: Senegal Negotiates Debt with Creditors for IMF Deal
item.description: Dakar is seeking an International Monetary Fund program to boost public finances by negotiating debt sustainability with creditors.

item.title: Armed bandits target Kisangani businesses amid rising insecurity
item.description: Civil society groups warn of increased home invasions and targeted attacks on business operators in Kabondo commune.

item.title: Ministry Honors First Agric Minister, Continues Reforms
item.description: The Ministry of Food and Agriculture recognized the foundational work of the late Ibrahim Adam, the first minister under Ghana's Fourth Republic.

item.title: Togo Environmentalist Séna Alouka Dies at 51
item.description: Tributes pour in across Africa for the tireless environmental defender who founded a major pan-African youth association.

item.title: Mauritania Well Exceeds Target Depth for Deep Water Exploration
item.description: The Ministry of Hydraulics and Sanitation announced that the Tintane experimental deep well has reached 518 meters, surpassing its 500-meter target.

item.title: Ghazouani receives OIC Secretary-General Ismaël Ould Cheikh Ahmed
item.description: The Mauritanian President met the newly elected OIC leader at his holiday residence in Assaba, acknowledging his unanimous election.

item.title: Ministry Denies Sponsoring Off-Brand Tourism Activities
item.description: Mauritania's Commerce and Tourism Ministry refutes claims of backing travel and media content that violates societal values.

item.title: French Father Seeks Children Blocked in Gabon
item.description: A French national has filed a complaint in Libreville seeking the return of his two children, who remain in Gabon with their Gabonese mother.

item.title: Government Projects Halt Amid E600 Million Cash Flow Crisis
item.description: Contractors, workers, and service delivery are impacted as approved funds for infrastructure projects remain unavailable, causing significant delays.

item.title: Eswatini Stock Exchange Launches Kwakhanya 2030 Strategy
item.description: The exchange aims to become a national engine for wealth creation and economic transformation by 2030.

item.title: Rail Operators Unite for Regional Logistics Showcase
item.description: Eswatini Railways joined forces with Transnet and Mozambique's rail authority to present integrated logistics solutions at the trade fair.

item.title: Bus Crash Kills Ten on Fogo Island
item.description: A bus carrying children fell about 30 meters in Campanas, Fogo, with rescue operations underway.

item.title: Agosto defeats Green Mamba 2-0 in CAF Confederation Cup first leg
item.description: Angolan side CD Primeiro De Agosto secured a significant first-leg advantage over Eswatini's Green Mamba in the TotalEnergies CAF Confederation Cup.

item.title: Senegalese Protest Rising Cost of Living
item.description: Hundreds marched in Dakar with empty baskets to protest widespread price increases on goods and services.

item.title: Nice draws with Le Mans, remains winless
item.description: OGC Nice drew 1-1 with Le Mans FC on Saturday, extending their winless streak in Ligue 1 to three matches.

item.title: South African golfer Leon Visser wins King's Golf Cup
item.description: Leon Visser secured the King's Golf Cup title with an 11-under-par performance in Eswatini, attracting global competitors.

item.title: Watchdog Accuses Malawi Govt of Genset Diesel Corruption
item.description: The Consumers Association of Malawi claims a plan to rent diesel generators is a scheme to enrich officials, not solve power outages.

item.title: EIB Funds Offshore Wind Study for Morocco
item.description: A two-year feasibility study will assess the technical and economic viability of Morocco's first offshore wind farm near Essaouira.

item.title: Algerian Jet Links Chad and Niger Amidst Regional Tensions
item.description: An Algerian government Gulfstream IV-SP made a discreet flight connecting N’Djamena, Niamey, and Algeria on Friday, September 4, 2026, fueling speculation about diplomatic.

item.title: Aiglons FC Held to 0-0 Draw by Sidama Bunna in CAF Champions League Opener
item.description: Chad's Aiglons FC dominated possession and created chances but could not score against Ethiopia's Sidama Bunna in the first leg of their CAF Champions League preliminary round.

item.title: Burundi Police Detain Congolese Refugees in Gitega
item.description: Authorities conducted document checks in urban areas where refugees had relocated for schooling, leading to several arrests.

item.title: Mother Suspected of Killing Child, Attempting Suicide in Burundi
item.description: A mother is suspected of killing her infant and then attempting suicide in Rumonge province, southwest Burundi.

item.title: Burundi President Awards Military Berets to Reserve Force Recruits
item.description: President Évariste Ndayishimiye attended a ceremony in Kigarika where 231 members of the FRAD completed three months of military training.

item.title: Journalist operated on while in police custody
item.description: Mohamed Yousfi underwent emergency surgery for appendicitis during his detention, raising concerns about his post-operative care.

item.title: POLISARIO Demands Spain Fulfill Decolonization Role
item.description: The POLISARIO Front calls on Spain to assume its legal, historical, and moral responsibilities in Western Sahara's decolonization process.

item.title: CFP-MEB Sells Saplings to Boost Burkina Faso's Greening Efforts
item.description: The Center for Professional Training in Emerging Trades is offering trees from 500 FCFA until September 30 to encourage planting.

item.title: Mauritania Envoy Attends Arab League Meeting
item.description: Ambassador Al-Hussein Sidi Abdallah Die participated in the 166th ordinary session of the Arab League Council in Cairo.

item.title: Western Powers Accused of Fueling Terrorism in Sahel
item.description: Analysts claim Western nations use geopolitical tools to destabilize hostile regimes and weaken rivals, with arms flowing to African groups.

item.title: Cacao Sector Faces Crisis, Union Warns
item.description: The Ivory Coast cacao sector is experiencing significant turbulence, according to a recent union statement.

item.title: Truck Hits and Kills Motorbike Taxi Driver in Lambanyi
item.description: A young motorbike taxi driver died after being struck by a truck carrying coal sacks on Saturday afternoon.

item.title: Greece Announces 2.2 Billion Euros in Aid and Tax Relief for 2027
item.description: Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis unveiled a package aimed at distributing economic growth benefits while maintaining fiscal stability.

item.title: Power Dynamos Lose Champions League Opener to Al Merrikh
item.description: Zambian champions Power Dynamos conceded a 37th-minute penalty in their CAF Champions League debut, resulting in a 1-0 defeat against Al Merrikh.

item.title: Health Ministry Incinerates Over 20 Containers of Dangerous Products
item.description: Health Minister Khaïté Sall oversaw the destruction of confiscated medical supplies deemed unfit for consumption at Kagbelen Dry Port.

item.title: Morocco Criminalizes Digital Election Interference
item.description: New electoral rules target fake news, unauthorized image use, and privacy breaches with prison sentences and fines.

item.title: Mali weather events cause thirteen deaths, affect nearly three thousand
item.description: Intensified rainfall and violent winds have resulted in thirteen fatalities and seventeen injuries since the start of the rainy season.

item.title: Caravan promotes national unity in Maradi
item.description: A national awareness and mobilization campaign visited Maradi to foster unity and patriotism among civilians and security forces.

item.title: Morocco Mandates New Rules for Electric Scooters and E-Bikes
item.description: New regulations define electric scooters and assisted-pedal bicycles, while public security vehicles are exempt from speed monitoring devices.

item.title: President Faye Urges Mayors to Prioritize Quality of Life
item.description: President Bassirou Diomaye Faye called on local authorities to integrate urban beautification and public well-being into their core responsibilities.

item.title: Algerian Football Federation Appoints New Coaching Staff
item.description: The Algerian Football Federation has appointed a new interim coaching staff, mirroring a similar situation from 1996.

item.title: Boss Mustapha Marks Seven Decades of Service
item.description: A prayer for continued health, wisdom, and impact marks the milestone birthday of a Nigerian public servant.

item.title: Bus stations record 19 injured and two dead in two years
item.description: Minister Osman Mahomed reported 19 accidents with injuries and two fatalities at ten bus stations since January 2024.

item.title: Ambulances Out of Service Hamper Health Ministry Fleet
item.description: Twenty-five of sixty-five ambulances are unavailable for service, with five deemed irreparable.

item.title: Officials Praise VDP Farmers' Progress in Bougouriba
item.description: A government mission observed agricultural advancements and challenges faced by youth volunteers in Bondigui, aiming to boost food self-sufficiency.

item.title: Parties Open Candidacy for Local Elections Amidst Exclusion Fears
item.description: Political parties have officially opened candidate nominations for upcoming local elections, emphasizing competence and experience to avoid past disqualifications.

item.title: Fire Kills 22 at Kinshasa Wedding Hall
item.description: A wedding reception in Kinshasa ended in tragedy with at least 22 deaths and multiple injuries after a fire swept through a party hall.

item.title: Three Algerian Consuls Arrive in France, Ambassador's Return Delayed
item.description: Algeria has completed its consular representation in France with three new appointments, though the ambassador's return remains postponed amid ongoing bilateral tensions.

item.title: Prosecutor Seeks 10 Years for ALRIM Corruption Defendants
item.description: Algerian state enterprise ALRIM faces allegations of squandering public funds, abuse of office, and contract violations in a Rouiba Court trial.

item.title: Tanzania Strengthens Anti-Money Laundering Systems
item.description: The nation has made significant progress in combating financial crimes, with ongoing legislative amendments to further bolster its financial sector.

item.title: CNSS Inspectors Find Many Unregistered Workers in Bars
item.description: The National Social Security Fund conducted checks on bars and drinking establishments, uncovering widespread non-compliance with worker registration.

item.title: MTN Ghana webinar urges SMEs to embrace financial discipline
item.description: Entrepreneurs are advised to separate personal and business finances and utilize digital tools for better cash flow management.

item.title: Egypt Agency Targets Global Markets for SMEs at China Fair
item.description: Egypt's Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency is showcasing domestic products at the China International Small and Medium Enterprises Fair to boost international.

item.title: Egypt Joins EU Project to Link Technical Training to Job Market
item.description: The AlignVET project, funded by the EU's Erasmus+ programme, aims to develop vocational curricula based on industry needs.

item.title: Morocco sardine catches decline, impacting European supply chains
item.description: Declining sardine stocks off Morocco, exacerbated by climate change and export restrictions, are causing shortages in German supermarkets.

item.title: Egyptian Banking Net Foreign Assets Increased in July
item.description: The Central Bank of Egypt reported a rise in net foreign assets to $28.418bn, equivalent to EGP 1.454trn, in July 2026.

item.title: Canyon Resources Exits ASX Top 500 Index
item.description: The Australian developer of Cameroon's Minim-Martap bauxite project will be removed from the All Ordinaries index on September 21.

item.title: Cosmetics Sale Becomes Agnibilékrou's Top Commercial Event
item.description: The weekly 'mardi mardi' market, which began with cosmetic products, now draws crowds and surpasses the traditional Friday market.

item.title: Drones kill two soldiers in Colombian garrison attack
item.description: Explosive-laden drones struck an army base in Ocaña, with the president blaming a rebel group.

item.title: Floods, poverty worsen child vulnerability in Mozambique
item.description: Sixteen thousand children in Gaza province face risks from floods, poverty, and cultural factors, prompting a government and partner investment.

item.title: Cavally Leader Outlines Development Gains and Challenges
item.description: Anne Désirée Ouloto-Lamizana highlighted infrastructure progress in education, electrification, and health in the Cavally region.

item.title: Daloa Becomes Exam Center for Agricultural Training Institute
item.description: The city of Daloa will host entrance exams for the National Institute of Professional Agricultural Training, decentralizing the process from Abidjan.

item.title: Ex-spy chief accuses Somali speaker of directing drone strike
item.description: Fahad Yasin claims Abdulkadir Mohamed Nur, also known as "Jama," ordered the attack on General Mahad Abdirahman Aden's residence.

item.title: Kasaï-Oriental Girls Married Before 18
item.description: Nearly half of girls in Kasaï-Oriental are married before turning 18, a situation that compromises their future and health.

item.title: Parliamentary Union Suspends Staff Union Activities
item.description: The General Secretary of the National Assembly cited an expired mandate and political interference as reasons for the suspension.

item.title: Gabon Mental Health Center Overwhelmed, Seeks Family Support
item.description: The National Mental Health Center in Mélen faces overcrowding due to insufficient beds and a call for increased family involvement in patient care and reintegration.

item.title: Health Union Protests Foreign Medical Staff Imports
item.description: The Health Sector Movement Union opposes the Tripoli government's plan to hire 200 Syrian medical and paramedical workers.

item.title: N'Djamena Councilors Boycott Budget Session Over Development Plan Dispute
item.description: Municipal councilors in N'Djamena's 9th arrondissement refused to review the revised budget, demanding a prior extraordinary session on the communal development plan.

item.title: Bolivia Barracks Blast Kills Two, Injures 81
item.description: An explosion at a military barracks in Viacha, Bolivia, has killed at least two people and injured 81 others, with fears the death toll may rise.

item.title: Red Lions, Masters Draw After Late Drama
item.description: Neither Red Lions nor Masters FC could find a goal in a goalless FDH Premiership match at Zomba Stadium.

item.title: Comic Art Festival Highlights Congolese Wealth and Struggle
item.description: The 7th African Comic Art and Music Festival in Kinshasa will feature the work of Alfred Liyolo and focus on the theme "Life, Nothing But Life."

item.title: Truck insurance validity questioned in fatal accident trial
item.description: A court in Dubréka is examining the insurance policy of a truck involved in a July 30 accident that killed three people.

item.title: Parliament's Lack of Opposition Raises Concerns for Public Representation
item.description: A debate is underway regarding the risk of a single-party national assembly and whether this absence of strong contradiction weakens the voice of the people.

item.title: Dodoma Grape Farmers Increase Harvest Sevenfold With Bank Support
item.description: Matumbulu farmers boosted annual production from 70 to 480 tonnes on 170 acres with financing and technical aid from TADB.

item.title: Cholera Outbreak Kills Six in Kasongo Health Zone
item.description: Six deaths were recorded in 24 hours amid 35 cholera cases in the Kasongo health zone, with local facilities lacking essential supplies.

item.title: Levante rejects Schalke 04 bid for Karl Etta Eyong
item.description: The Spanish club deemed the German team's offer insufficient for the Cameroonian forward valued at 15 million euros.

item.title: US Forces Destroy Three Iranian Oil Tankers
item.description: American forces permanently disabled two tankers and "completely destroyed" a third in the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea.

item.title: Drone strike damages Tripoli fuel tanks
item.description: A drone strike early Thursday hit two fuel tanks and pipeline lines at the Tripoli oil depot, but officials stated operations remain normal.

item.title: Morocco Subsidizes Soft Wheat Imports Amid Global Price Hikes
item.description: The government will offer a flat subsidy on imported soft wheat to bolster national reserves as global prices surge due to Black Sea tensions.

item.title: Study Finds Uneducated Youth Lack Sexual Health Information
item.description: A recent study in Burundi's Ngozi district reveals that a significant majority of out-of-school adolescents have never heard of sexual and reproductive health services.

item.title: UNITA Pledges Patriotic Front for 2027 Power Alternation
item.description: The party's Permanent Committee urged increased voter registration efforts in rural and disadvantaged areas ahead of the general election.

item.title: Promoter Uses Culture for Social Good in Chad
item.description: Héritier Evariste Ngaralbaye champions Chadian music to support solidarity, education, and humanitarian actions.

item.title: Amnesty International Criticizes EU Migrant Hub Plans in Uganda
item.description: Amnesty International has raised serious human rights concerns over proposed EU migrant return hubs in Uganda and Rwanda.
